messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: CDF values > 1
parts:
Thanks for reporting. I'm cc-ing stan-dev.

Can we change the behavior of the CDFs to
do this internally without changing their derivatives?
That way we can have the best of both worlds.

The problem with the proposed solution

> otherResponseCDF <- if_else(otherResponseCDF>1,1,otherResponseCDF);

is that when the condition is true, you lose the connection
to the derivative. This may not be apparent in a large model,
but it's not the right thing to do.

- Bob

On 6/25/13 7:55 PM, Mike Lawrence wrote:
> After a lot of playing around, it seems that the culprit is indeed the fact that "otherResponseCDF" is occasionally
> greater than 1, causing log1m() to throw an error. Actually, it's only ever minutely greater than 1 (ex. 1+1.04361e-14,
> 1+6.21725e-15, etc), so I suspect this is a precision issue of some sort (I'm only vaguely familiar with the idea that
> computers can have trouble representing numbers precisely) . Adding the line:
>
> otherResponseCDF <- if_else(otherResponseCDF>1,1,otherResponseCDF);
>
> solves things.
>
>
>
> On Tuesday, June 25, 2013 4:44:32 PM UTC-3, Mike Lawrence wrote:
>
> Thanks for the help (and apologies for failing to add a subject line!).
>
> I must be failing to properly constrain the range of one of the variables somewhere. I have to head out for a bit
> now, but I'll play some more this evening and report back to resolve the thread.
>
>
>
> On Tuesday, June 25, 2013 3:33:23 PM UTC-3, Ben Goodrich wrote:
>
> On Tuesday, June 25, 2013 1:57:44 PM UTC-4, Mike Lawrence wrote:
>
> Any suggestions as to what I should do next to track down what's going awry?
>
>
> It's the last line
>
> |
>
> |
> lp__ <- lp__ + (log1m(otherResponseCDF)+log(thisResponsePDF));
> |
>
> |
> log1m() requires its argument to be <= 1, which isn't guaranteed to be the case in your model. Actually, I think
> it is guaranteed to not be the case as written:
>
> |
>
> otherResponseCDF <- 1+(tmp1+tmp2)/thisStartMax[subject[i]];
>
> |
>
> If tmp1, tmp2, and thisStartMax[subject[i]] are all positive then otherResponseCDF is always going to greater
> than 1.
>
> Ben

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: [stan-users] Re: CDF values > 1
parts:
For a well defined model this should only happen rarely due to numerical issues.  Really, the solution is to try to fix the numerical issue with the model.  Beyond that though, it should have only a marginal impact on sampling in most cases.

Cheers,
Marcus
On Tue, Jun 25, 2013 at 10:23 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

Thanks for reporting.   I'm cc-ing stan-dev.

Can we change the behavior of the CDFs to
do this internally without changing their derivatives?
That way we can have the best of both worlds.

The problem with the proposed solution

>      otherResponseCDF <- if_else(otherResponseCDF>1,1,otherResponseCDF);

is that when the condition is true, you lose the connection
to the derivative.  This may not be apparent in a large model,
but it's not the right thing to do.

- Bob

On 6/25/13 7:55 PM, Mike Lawrence wrote:

After a lot of playing around, it seems that the culprit is indeed the fact that "otherResponseCDF" is occasionally
greater than 1, causing log1m() to throw an error. Actually, it's only ever minutely greater than 1 (ex. 1+1.04361e-14,
1+6.21725e-15, etc), so I suspect this is a precision issue of some sort (I'm only vaguely familiar with the idea that
computers can have trouble representing numbers precisely) . Adding the line:

     otherResponseCDF <- if_else(otherResponseCDF>1,1,otherResponseCDF);

solves things.



On Tuesday, June 25, 2013 4:44:32 PM UTC-3, Mike Lawrence wrote:

    Thanks for the help (and apologies for failing to add a subject line!).

    I must be failing to properly constrain the range of one of the variables somewhere. I have to head out for a bit
    now, but I'll play some more this evening and report back to resolve the thread.



    On Tuesday, June 25, 2013 3:33:23 PM UTC-3, Ben Goodrich wrote:

        On Tuesday, June 25, 2013 1:57:44 PM UTC-4, Mike Lawrence wrote:

            Any suggestions as to what I should do next to track down what's going awry?


        It's the last line

        |

        |
        lp__ <- lp__ + (log1m(otherResponseCDF)+log(thisResponsePDF));
        |

        |
        log1m() requires its argument to be <= 1, which isn't guaranteed to be the case in your model. Actually, I think
        it is guaranteed to not be the case as written:

        |

        otherResponseCDF <- 1+(tmp1+tmp2)/thisStartMax[subject[i]];

        |

        If tmp1, tmp2, and thisStartMax[subject[i]] are all positive then otherResponseCDF is always going to greater
        than 1.

        Ben
